n: Lehi turns to his youngest son, Joseph, born in the wilderness during Lehi’s hardest years.
Lehi prays that the Lord will dedicate this precious land as an inheritance for Joseph and his descendants alongside his brothers — if they keep the commandments.
Lehi blesses Joseph forever and promises that his descendants will never be completely destroyed.

f.w: thy seed shall not utterly be destroyed

n: Lehi reveals that he descends from Joseph who was sold into Egypt — through Manasseh — and that the Lord made great covenants with that ancient Joseph.

Joseph of Egypt saw the latter days and was promised that God would raise a righteous branch from his descendants — not the Messiah, but a branch broken off (Lehi’s family). Christ would reveal Himself to them in the last days, bringing them from darkness to light.

f.w: a branch which was to be broken off

n: Joseph prophesied of a “choice seer” whom the Lord would raise up from his descendants. Latter-day Saints understand this seer to be Joseph Smith.

f.g: One who sees by divine power — a prophet who can reveal past and future.

n: The Lord told Joseph that this seer would be highly esteemed among Joseph’s descendants and would do a great work for them, teaching them God’s covenants with their fathers.

f.g: Joseph Smith’s inspired revision of the Bible (JST Genesis 50) restores a parallel version of this prophecy.

n: The seer will do only the work God commands, and God will make him great because he does God’s work.
He will be great like Moses, the deliverer of Israel.
Joseph of Egypt foresaw Moses, who would lead Israel out of Egypt.

f.w: deliver thy people out of the land of Egypt

n: The latter-day seer will bring forth God’s word to Joseph’s descendants — and also help convince them of the word they already have, the Bible.

Joseph’s descendants will write (the Book of Mormon), and Judah’s descendants will write (the Bible). These records will “grow together” to refute false doctrines, end contention, and bring peace and knowledge of God’s covenants.
The seer will be made strong out of weakness when God’s work of restoring Israel begins. Joseph Smith was an uneducated farm boy when called.

f.w: out of weakness he shall be made strong

n: Joseph prophesied that the Lord would bless the seer and confound those who tried to destroy him. Joseph of Egypt was certain this promise would be fulfilled.

f.w: they that seek to destroy him shall be confounded

n: The seer’s name would be Joseph, like his father’s — Joseph Smith Jr. was named after his father, Joseph Smith Sr. What he brings forth by God’s power will bring Joseph’s people to salvation.

f.w: his name shall be called after me

n: Joseph is as sure of this as of the promise about Moses. God promised to preserve his descendants forever.

f.w: I will preserve thy seed forever

n: God promised to raise a Moses with power in his rod and judgment in writing. Moses would not be eloquent, so God would write His law with His own finger and give Moses a spokesman — Aaron.

f.w: I will not make him mighty in speaking
by the finger of mine own hand

n: Likewise God would raise up the latter-day seer with a spokesman. The seer would write (translate) the record of Joseph’s descendants, and a spokesman would declare it. Latter-day revelation names Sidney Rigdon as a spokesman to Joseph Smith.

f.w: I will make for him a spokesman

n: The seer will write what God in His wisdom wants Joseph’s descendants to have. It will be as if their ancestors cried to them “from the dust” — an image of a voice from buried records.

f.w: cried unto them from the dust

n: These ancient voices will cry repentance to their descendants many generations later, and their message will go forth because of its simplicity.
Because of the ancient writers’ faith, God will make their weak words strong, to help their descendants remember His covenants.

f.w: the weakness of their words will I make strong

n: Lehi tells his son Joseph that this is how their ancestor prophesied.
Because of this covenant, young Joseph is blessed: his descendants will not be destroyed, because they will listen to the words of the book.
One mighty in word and deed will rise among them, an instrument in God’s hands with great faith, bringing much restoration to Israel. Many Latter-day Saints apply this, too, to Joseph Smith.

f.w: an instrument in the hands of God

n: Lehi tells young Joseph, still a child, to listen to his brother Nephi, and these blessings will be fulfilled. He asks Joseph to remember his dying father’s words.

f.w: hearken unto the words of thy brother, Nephi
